title: Remove the Defender
subtitle: Capture or chase away the guard, then take the prize.
goals: Combine deflection with the back rank

steps.say: When a target is guarded, don't give up — interrogate the guard. Can you capture it? Chase it? Overload it? Pin it? Remove the defender and the 'protected' piece is suddenly hanging. Every guard is a weakness wearing a uniform.

steps.prompt: You'd love Rxd8 — but the knight guards it. Deal with the guard FIRST!
hints: Rxd8 right now gets answered by Nxd8. So what if the knight disappeared first?
Your bishop can capture the defender — then the rook robs the house.

line.say: And the rook falls with check — for FREE this time. Bishop for knight and rook: a clean profit.

rejections.say: Nxd8! The knight was on guard duty and did its job. Remove the defender FIRST — Bxc6 — then take.

steps.wrongSay: The d8 rook has exactly one defender. What removes it?
steps.successSay: Guard first, treasure second — the order is the whole tactic.

steps.prompt: The f6 knight guards the d5 bishop — but the knight is PINNED. Prove its defense is fake!
hints: Your Bg5 pins the f6 knight against the queen. A pinned defender is no defender.
Take the d5 bishop. If the knight dares recapture, what happens to the queen?

line.say: Taking the 'defended' bishop — because the defense is an illusion!
The knight abandoned its pin duty and the queen fell instantly. Pinned pieces guard nothing.

rejections.say: gxf6 — you gave up the pin AND your bishop pair just to remove a guard that was already fake. Rxd5 wins the piece outright: the pinned knight never truly defended it.

steps.wrongSay: Recount d5's defenders — does a knight pinned to its queen really count?
steps.successSay: Pins turn defenders into spectators. Always re-audit the guards when a pin appears.

steps.prompt: Black's queen guards BOTH the e8 rook and the b5 knight. She can't do two jobs — overload her!
hints: Count the queen's duties: e8 needs her, b5 needs her. Force her to choose.
Capture one of her charges — when she recaptures, the other one is abandoned.

line.say: The queen must recapture — it's check!
And the knight she abandoned is free. One defender, two jobs — the classic overload.

rejections.say: Qxb5! You took the knight while it was still defended — the queen did her job and you lost a queen for a knight. Overload her with the CHECK first: Rxe8+.

steps.wrongSay: The queen is stretched between two duties. Which capture forces her to pick one?
steps.successSay: Overloaded defenders are everywhere — count DUTIES, not just defenders.

steps.prompt: The e8 rook is the ONLY guard of Black's back rank. Deflect it — with the most forcing sacrifice on the board!
hints: If the e8 rook vanishes, your rook mates on e8. What forces it to vanish?
Give your QUEEN on e8. The recapture is forced — and then the back rank belongs to your rook.

line.say: Queen sacrifice! The rook must be recaptured by the queen — it's the only legal reply...
CHECKMATE. The defender was deflected, the back rank collapsed, and the queen sac cost you nothing at all. This exact combination decides thousands of real games.

rejections.say: A slow threat Black can meet. You have a forced mate in two: remove the back-rank guard by force — Qxe8+!!

steps.wrongSay: Black's whole position hangs on one rook. The most forcing move in chess is a capture with check...
steps.successSay: Deflection + back rank: the queen sacrifice that every tactician dreams of playing. Now it's in your arsenal.
